intro: Professionals and everyday users convert degrees (°) to radians (rad) when working across other and si standards in CNC rotary indexing, optical alignment, trigonometric engineering, and surveying bearings. One degree equals 0.017453 radians, while 1 radian equals 57.29578 degrees. Whether you are verifying angle specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Exact NIST Factor vs. Early Rounding Drift
items: The exact conversion factor from Degree to Radian is 0.01745329, derived from the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement (1 inch = 25.4 mm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg).

In structural engineering, CNC machining, or bulk inventory totals, rounding the multiplier to 2 decimal places too early can introduce cumulative tolerance errors; always compute with the full factor and round only the final displayed figure.

faqs.question: How many radians (rad) are in 1 degree (°)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.01745329 radians (rad) in 1 degree (°), which rounds to 0.0175 rad for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 radian equals 57.29578 degrees.

faqs.question: How do I convert degrees to radians (° to rad)?
faqs.answer: To convert degrees to radians, use the formula: rad = ° × 0.01745329. For example, converting 90 ° gives 1.5708 rad.

faqs.question: What is 90 degrees in radians?
faqs.answer: 90 degrees (°) equals exactly 1.5708 radians (rad) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
